independence.method: Independent analytic derivation and exact integer/Fraction constant and remainder checks; no fitting, truth use or sweeps.

findings.finding: For fixed chronological inputs, differentiating f'= -lambda(f-c) yields f_alpha'= -lambda f_alpha -lambda sum_{l=1}^{alpha_j} binom(alpha_j,l) g_{alpha-l e_j}. All nonzero lambda derivatives are pure in the active log-rate direction and equal lambda. c is parameter independent; switch times produce no parameter-boundary derivatives. Finite ordered affine compositions are smooth for positive rates, so the differentiated finite-prefix equations are valid. The same integrating-factor argument applies to integrable fixed sign inputs with finite directional throughput.

F lies in [0,1] and u lies in [-1,1] by positive affine transport, hence |F|<=1 and |u-s|<=2 during active intervals. For y(0)=0 and y'=-lambda y-lambda q, |y(T)|<=sup|q| integral_0^T exp(-integral_r^T lambda)lambda(r)dr=sup|q|(1-exp(-integral_0^T lambda)). This is valid across any fixed chronological reversals. At rest lambda=0 and all derivative states persist. Induction in total derivative order gives the stated global constants without multiplying a bound by the number of switches or resetting derivatives.

The recurrence gives C10=C01=1, C20=C02=3, C11=1, C30=C03=13 and C21=C12=3. In particular the (2,1) forcing is 2 f11+f01 during plus input and f20 during minus input, both bounded by 3 for F and 6 for u. Inactive-direction forcing is zero but its carried derivative still decays. Thus mixed derivatives are covered without assuming commutative forced transport or an exposure-total summary.

Along r -> r*t, the third directional derivative has multinomial coefficients 1,3,3,1. Integrating the degree-two remainder gives C30 p^3/6+C21 p^2 m/2+C12 p m^2/2+C03 m^3/6 times S. For each gradient component, first-order Taylor of that component has second derivative equal to the corresponding third response derivatives; integration gives the stated two quadratic bounds. The straight log-rate segment remains in the positive-rate domain. No differentiation of an absolute error inequality is used.

Linearity vH=B F+H u and H>=0 imply S=|B|+2H. Holding independent log rates and the other amplitude fixed, partial_B(vH-P) is the free-response remainder and partial_H(vH-P) is the forced-response remainder, hence S=1 and S=2 respectively. A uniform amplitude-domain bound needs finite amplitude bounds. Dependent solver coordinates, including Q in both gamma/Q rates or parameter-dependent initial state, require the complete chain rule; H6 correctly limits its direct claim to independent amplitudes/rates.

The bounds are stationary exact-input/exact-arithmetic response statements, independent of duration, sample count and minimum interval. They do not control floating-point accumulation, aging, polynomial state support, posterior fidelity, fit displacement or coverage. P3/M1 can consume the value/derivative bounds only with their additional common-chart, whitening, reference-precision and likelihood premises; H6 describes this as a route rather than automatic qualification. No evidence discount, truncation, support restriction or chart reset is justified.

acceptance_scope: Conditional exact-arithmetic mathematical proof of duration-uniform pure/mixed stationary hysteresis log-rate derivative majorants and local Taylor value, rate-gradient and independent-amplitude remainders for fixed chronological inputs. H5/H1 are reviewed dependencies for this claim; no separate implementation, finite-results, hardware, physical-coverage or lifetime qualification is implied.
